subject: Social Studies
title: Finding the Real Cause and the Real Effect — Step by Step
tipLine: Order in the passage isn't always the order events happened — this is about tracking that.

vocabTerms.definition: the event or condition that makes something else happen
what happens as a result of the cause

blocks.heading: Ask which one depends on the other
blocks.body: The cause can exist without the effect, but the effect can't happen without the cause. When a passage says one thing "led to," "resulted in," or "caused" another, find the event on each side of that phrase — the trigger is the cause, what follows from it is the effect. Watch out for details that are true but describe neither — background information isn't automatically a cause or an effect.

blocks.heading: Worked example
blocks.body: "After a severe drought destroyed crops across the region, thousands of farming families migrated to cities looking for work." What's the cause? The drought — it's the trigger. What's the effect? Families migrating to cities — that's what happened as a result. Neither depends on "the region" or "crops" alone; those are just context inside the cause.

blocks.question: "When the price of oil spiked in the 1970s, many Americans switched to smaller, more fuel-efficient cars." What was the effect described here?
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right — the price spike is the cause; switching to fuel-efficient cars is what resulted from it.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Close — that one is the cause (or just a time period), not the result. The effect is what happened because of the price spike: the switch to fuel-efficient cars.
